To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the ResNet-38 architecture, trained from scratch, integrating non-image features achieves the best results for the considered pathology classification task.

(1) the performance of ResNet-38 is comparable to ResNet-101 and ResNet-50; (2) the inclusion of patient age and gender in the classification process leads to an improvement in performance; and (3) the inclusion of acquisition type information leads to a decrease in performance.
the X-ray specific ResNet-38 network outperforms the other networks and integrating non-image information improves the overall performance.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a systematic investigation of different approaches for multi-label X-ray classification.
the investigation of the performance of different approaches to chest X-ray pathology classification, and the analysis of the resulting classification process.
the development of an optimized deep learning-based approach for the multi-label classification of chest X-ray data.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
a ResNet-38 architecture, trained on the ChestX-ray14 training set, fine-tuned on the validation set and integrated with non-image data, achieves the best results in terms of AUC and ROC statistics.
there is no best network, but the best approach is to use a ResNet-50 with a depth of 38, and integrate non-image features in the classification process.
there is no single best approach, and the optimal approach depends on the dataset and the application.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the integration of non-image data in the classification process is crucial, and that the ResNet-38 architecture yields the best overall performance.
the integration of non-image data into a deep learning approach can be beneficial for chest X-ray classification.
there is a need to further investigate the use of non-image data in the classification process, which can be used to improve the performance.
The main takeaway from our work is that
there is no clear winner in the investigated classification tasks.

the choice of network architecture has a strong impact on the achieved classification results, and that a combination of different network architectures and non-image features yields the best results.
a careful selection of the network architecture is crucial for the classification performance.
